title: Killer baseline
text: Killer baseline The creator's verdict after the September 14 near-full-lobby playtest was that the killers were too easy: running away always worked, because pursuit ran at 3.25 m/s against a 4.3 m/s player run. The September 15 pressure pass raises pursuit with the crew, adds a close lunge, makes worksite doors part of the chase and re-rolls field obstacles every stop. The September 20 pass adds gradual footsteps, cover attenuation, partial-exposure suspicion and warned lethal commitments. These are accepted starting values, not measured balance. Sensing and search tuning Killer Walk hearing Run hearing Search budget Search points Chase fatigue Groundskeeper 5 m 12 m 22 s 6 30 s Rattletrap 12 m 26 m 26 s 7 32 s Roadkill 2 m 8 m 18 s 5 26 s Hitchhiker 3 m 10 m 16 s 5 24 s Usher 1 m 6 m 22 s 6 30 s Switchboard 4 m 11 m 24 s 6 32 s Hound 2 m 8 m 16 s, capped by the trail's expiry 5 24 s Mimic 1 m 6 m 14 s 4 20 s Warden 2 m 9 m 14 s shared search from the last evidence 4 20 s Deadeye 1 m 7 m 12 s shared search from the last evidence 4 18 s Values are the code's ( SpookKiller._ConfigureRoster , _ConfigurePursuit , _ConfigureCommitment , 2026-09-24). The search budget is an ordinary, uncommitted search; the chase fatigue is how long a hunter that has confirmed you keeps its commitment after its last sighting (below). Movement sensing uses horizontal speed. Ordinary killers ignore speeds up to 0.9 m/s; Rattletrap starts above 0.55 m/s. Radius interpolates from zero to the walking value at 2.7 m/s, then to the running value at 4.3 m/s. Cover multiplies the radius by 0.25 for ordinary hearing and 0.65 for Rattletrap. Detection distance is spherical. Soft Soles multiplies movement ranges by 0.75. Safe, downed/ineligible, and suspended players are excluded. This does not inspect microphone input. Visible and audible candidates are distinct. Vision takes priority; sound behind cover starts investigation without granting sight-only warnings/attacks. New sound evidence refreshes at most every 0.8 seconds. When a player becomes quiet or leaves hearing range, the last evidence and deadline stop following them. Rattletrap remains blind, with the largest movement ranges and separate task-noise investigation. Usher investigates after a broken warning and must warn afresh when it visually reacquires. Sight samples head and torso separately. Full exposure confirms immediately; one visible sample accumulates suspicion for 0.5 seconds, with slow decay behind full cover. Escape Artist (level 10) extends this to 1.1 seconds and scales visual searches to 65%, without shortening sound searches. Trailbreaker separately scales footstep-evidence searches to 65%; it does not shorten visual searches. Repair noise uses cover attenuation and Silent Tools halves its range. Hitchhiker ambush focus uses visible targets or evidence less than six seconds old, never hidden live positions. Roadkill charges execute. Hitchhiker and Usher warn for two seconds before a six-second lethal commitment against the warned player; breaking sight cancels it. Expiry gives two seconds of recovery and requires a new warning. Session elimination uses synced identities to survive re-registration and leaves the quota seat intact. Actual Udon tests cover these paths; uploaded migration and physical input acceptance remain separate. Turning corners and searching Observed movement can project a short continuation, bounded to five metres. Mode 6 searches alternate nearby reachable NavMesh probes with authored route anchors. Missing route anchors no longer cause instant abandonment. Searches have both time and point budgets, so the configured duration is a ceiling rather than a guaranteed wait. A search pause is a 1.5-second look (0.8 s while committed) in which the body holds its route heading and only the head turns, within each killer's look limit (18-52°); the head, not a sweep oscillator, drives vision and presentation. Synced checkpoint fields preserve probe position, progress, reference heading, and sensing state. Chase commitment (2026-09-24) A confirmed sighting locks the hunter onto that player until it tires. For that player only: sight range x1.5 and the half-cone +25°, movement and click hearing x1.6 (Rattletrap x1.2) with cover muffling 0.6 instead of 0.25 (Rattletrap 0.85), a 4-second peek grace, and 6 m of priority over a nearer stranger. On losing sight the hunter runs the hidden leg its observed heading predicts: seven navmesh probes 8 m past the last seen point, a candidate hidden from the hunter's eye yet in clear sight of that point, with a route no longer than the way there plus 11 m; to the last seen point, around the corner, once more along the leg (6 s per leg, two legs; a further turn is a point hidden from the last seen point yet in sight of the corner just rounded; open ground predicts no corner and goes straight to the search), then a search that lasts until the fatigue above, at chase pace, with 0.8-second looks and four extra sites centred on the corner. The quarry's own footsteps, click, lit lamp or scent re-aim it and push the deadline to at least 8 s ahead; a stranger's evidence counts only when nearer than the quarry's latest point or within 6 m of the hunter. The hidden player's live position is never read: the corner is inferred and hearing reports a 2 m grid. The refuge, a decoy, the end of the round and an ownership handoff clear the lock; a stun or flash only interrupts it, and Hitchhiker and Usher warn again for a full 2 s on every reacquire, and only from plain sight: a quarry reacquired through the longer locked reach is closed on first. Escape Artist and Trailbreaker scale the commitment as they do a search. Rattletrap locks by hearing; Hound rounds corners by scent; Warden and Deadeye commit through the gun loop. See Docs/ChaseCommitment-2026-09-24.md . Leaving camp after an escape (2026-09-24) A locked quarry who makes the refuge while the hunter or its last known point is within 30 m of the refuge box (every distance here is measured flat from the box's edge, in the zone's own frame, so yawed Calder and School sites read correctly) sends the hunter back out. The check runs once a think ahead of both brains, so Warden and Deadeye get it too; a warning, a charge or a disguise finishes first and reaches it through its recovery, and a Usher or Mimic whose warned target makes it drops the warning the same way. The hunter clears the lock and runs an ordinary search centred on an open patrol anchor at least 35 m out, the one nearest a point 45 m from the refuge centre along its field axis leaning toward the side the hunter came from (10 m of jitter, at most three path checks, a 30 m fallback), at search pace with no fresh evidence, for 30 s ( lastSense 5). Its senses stay on: anyone it sees or hears outside the step-out ring is hunted as usual, which ends the withdrawal. For 15 s anyone within 12 m of the refuge is sheltered from its senses, its lock and its blows; for 60 s patrol points and Hitchhiker warps keep 30 m away. Always, whatever happened: no patrol point, search probe, lead, anchor or final hold, disguise, Deadeye reposition, Switchboard hazard or recovery bind lands within 12 m of the refuge (a search that would hold there ends instead). The Hound only follows scent laid after the escape, and a pending Deadeye reposition is dropped. The windows travel in the synced campTimes array; the hidden player's position is never read beyond the same refuge test the lock already uses. See Docs/CampWithdraw-2026-09-24.md . Speed, lunges and the cost of a hit Pursuit is a multiple of the players' base run speed and patrol a multiple of their base walk speed (2.7 / 4.3 m/s), and both rise linearly with the crew to +20% at eight or more participants. The crew count is the stop's locked count lowered by departures, so late joiners never speed a hunter up mid-stop. Killer Solo pursuit 4 crew 8+ crew Groundskeeper, Usher 4.52 4.90 5.42 Rattletrap, Roadkill, Switchboard 4.30 4.67 5.16 Hitchhiker, Mimic 4.73 5.14 5.68 Hound 4.64 5.04 5.57 Warden 3.66 3.97 4.39 Deadeye 3.23 3.50 3.87 Values are metres per second, rounded; committed charges and attacks have their own timing. Solo patrol is 2.70 m/s for the original six, 2.97 for Hound, 2.16 for Mimic/Warden and 2.43 for Deadeye, with the same crew factor. Shared melee pursuit has a close lunge and a 1.5-second recovery after a landed ordinary hit. Gun killers use confirmation, committed aim and reload windows rather than contact damage. Players run 4.3 m/s before items and perks. Faster melee hunters reward cover, doors and interruption; ranged hunters instead make distance, warning timing, sidesteps and solid cover matter. Cargo slows players without Courier. Judge these interactions in real play rather than treating the speed table as a complete difficulty model. Doors and per-stop layouts Worksite front openings have hinged doors. Crew open and close them; the owner validates distance, eligibility, a cooldown and whether anyone stands in the doorway or the leaf's swing. Doors deliberately do not carve navigation: a hunter stops at a closed leaf, opens it in 0.8 s when unhurried, and bashes it off its hinge in 1.2 s while pursuing or following fresh evidence — a broken door stays open for the rest of the stop, so a door buys distance once and cannot be looped. Rear openings stay clear as a second exit. Every stop attempt also rolls a fresh set of field obstacles (hay bales, stalled vehicles, log piles, crates, drums, a trailer). Solid parts carve the navigation mesh at runtime, and after each roll the owner verifies that the configured patrol, cargo, repair and supply destinations remain reachable, re-rolling twice and then falling back to a clear field. The spectator map draws the active obstacles and closed doors over its baked terrain. Presentation and debug surfaces The world killer model and spectator map use the same always-active feed. Non-owners wait for a matching pose, snap on the first valid sample/round change, then interpolate nearby updates. Feed data includes warning/hazard/decoy state and hearing ranges. The map’s gold vision outline is clipped against cover; blue rings show walking/running hearing. The legend also reports the hunter's current speed and crew factor, and the map draws gray blocks for the rolled obstacles and cream bars for closed doors, so a watcher sees the same field the crew is in. Explicit sorting keeps them above terrain. Only eligible dispatch spectators can view tracking. The map is a horizontal projection, so vertical cover and actual head visibility can differ. Host → AI diagnostics is an optional independent reader for owner IDs, heartbeat age, path state, feed receipt, presentation readiness, and movement information. It now reports Killer v4 with the current speed, landed hits, lunges and doors opened or broken; the owner logs the same line on mode changes and every ten seconds. Mode 7 is “at a door”. Radar visibility and diagnostics are development features; decide whether to remove or restrict them before release. Specialist encounters The ten-killer roster retains one active killer. SpookEncounterAI owns specialist evidence and ranged commitment while SpookKiller owns shared navigation, doors, pose and interruptions. Hound records bounded movement breadcrumbs, waits at least 1.5 seconds before investigating them, and expires them after 12 seconds (five with Trailbreaker). It does not refresh its search by rereading one breadcrumb. Mimic uses a separate false-cargo mesh, breathing motion and positional creaks. Proximity reveal requires visible, unsmoked body evidence and a 1.6-second warning; real objective cargo is untouched. Warden confirms sight for 0.45 seconds, warns for 1.8 seconds and locks the last 0.55 seconds. Its 14-metre shotgun fan is lethal and followed by a 3.2-second reload. Deadeye confirms for 0.8 seconds, warns for 2.5 seconds and locks the last 0.7 seconds. Its 38-metre rifle is lethal, reloads for four seconds and selects a reachable lateral firing position when available. Gun searches use frozen sight/sound positions with the shared search budget (14 s Warden, 12 s Deadeye), or the chase fatigue after a sighting. Escape Artist and Trailbreaker shorten the corresponding search or commitment by 35 percent. Expiry releases the old navigation path. Decoys and successful stuns clear continuous visual confirmation; accepted repair noise is consumed once. Cover blocks actual shot rays; smoke blocks acquisition and pre-commit aim only. Ownership recovery cancels pending shots instead of replaying them. Specialist presentation uses attempt-keyed synced arrays for stage, deadlines, muzzle/aim points, shot serial and trails. The receiving-client fixture decodes those arrays through the ClientSim SDK codec, alongside the normal pose feed; uploaded transport and device acceptance are still separate gates. Deferred work and acceptance Fair search persistence and pressure distribution for solo through 16 participants; whether the 20-32 s chase commitment and its boosted senses read as fair solo ( chaseFatigueSeconds , chaseSightScale , chaseHearingScale are the first values to lower). Human evasion across multiple corners, noisy work, decoys, and changing routes; a second hidden turn or a double-back must stay counterplay. Roadkill charge visibility versus actual hits under latency. Hitchhiker warp presentation and safe relocation tells. Switchboard hazard cover rules, warning/active distinction, and alternate escape routes. Unreachable targets with reachable alternatives and owner changes in every mode. Cooldown/stun immunity and strong-perk builds without unavoidable chains. Whether the new speeds are fair rather than merely hard. crewSpeedBonus and the per-killer chaseSpeedRatios are the first inspector values to lower if a chase reads as unavoidable. Door agreement across clients and after owner migration, and the stop-start navigation carve cost on Quest and iPhone. The local lanes cover navigation, frozen evidence, hearing boundaries/perks, search expiry, synced metadata, and rendered rings/cones. The fresh uploaded fairness and migration matrix remains open.

title: Environment & art direction
text: Environment & art direction The three destinations and dispatch now contain dressed original environment assets. The September 20 pass adds four original specialist-killer models and warning sounds, darker baked dispatch interiors, faulty fixture glow, distance fog and a lounge CRT with a fake projected beam. Final presentation and mobile performance still need physical-device review. Campfire as a gameplay anchor The protective lantern and covered van refuge are the dependable destination in every stop. Make their warm silhouette readable from escape routes. Preserve generous access and standing room for the crew; do not turn the entrance into a narrow collision trap. Since the 2026-09-24 revamp the van has a walkable interior : its floor, roof and outer walls are solid (simple box colliders), while the bench, locker, chairs, monitor console, bulkhead and every door leaf are walk-through, and the two cab doors open on a click for everyone. Steps under the barn doors, the cab doors and the rear bumper lead in. The covered exterior under the camp tent stays the main protected space, so keep its capacity. The model is unpainted starter paint for now; the livery, rust and stencils follow the paint brief in Docs/VanRevamp-2026-09-24.md . Three destinations to playtest Area Existing foundation Next design questions Camp Deadwood Cabin/shed/shelter shapes and wooded routes Which loops create a second escape option? Where can the van lantern be glimpsed? Which shelters allow readable corner searches? Last Chance Service Station Pumps, canopy/garage/store and vehicle cover How do open forecourt risk and close service corridors differ? Can every job be approached from more than one direction? Calder laboratory Multilevel industrial laboratory, reactor spaces and tiered routes Are vertical travel, distant warnings and escape routes readable in fog and low light? Aim for roughly 15–25 seconds of travel from the van to ordinary work sites. This is a design target to measure, not a claim that every current route meets it. Compact solo routes should remain interesting; larger crews need additional useful work sites, not just more repeated walking. Per-stop layouts and doors Each area has a Randomized layout root. Its children are sites; each site's children are the mutually exclusive variants one stop can roll — hay rows, stacked bales, stalled vehicles, fallen pines, log stacks, crates and pallets, a tractor, oil drums, a jackknifed trailer, a collapsed sign, tire stacks. The original outdoor layout seed had 11 sites with 29 variants; that is a historical seed count, not a current whole-scene asset count. Replace their meshes freely and add sites of your own; any geometry works, with solid parts on layer 11. Per site, emptyWeight sets how often nothing appears, variantWeights follow child order, and a positive routeGroup keeps at least one site of that group clear so several blockers can cross one corridor without sealing it. Keep obstacles at least 1.2 m clear of anchors and patrol points and 3 m clear of the refuge — the validator enforces it. Worksite front openings carry a hinged door: a frame, a leaf that swings inward, and an interaction trigger. Keep the leaf a single solid collider under the hinge and the doorway at least 1.2 m wide; the killer's agent is 0.9 m across. Rear openings must stay clear — supply anchors sit in them, and a cabin whose only two exits could both close is a dead end. After any of this, run SpookCo → Apply gameplay scene additions , which adds carving obstacles, keeps the new geometry out of the navigation bake and the spectator map texture, rebuilds navigation when static geometry changed, and re-collects the layout. Then run Validate scene and rules , which fails on a site with no variants, a variant that would block an anchor or the refuge, a mis-wired door, and a doorway the baked mesh cannot pass through. Re-bake lighting after adding static geometry such as door frames. Objective and round design Make cargo destinations, repair states, shared supplies, and extraction unmistakable through shape and feedback, not color alone. Retain interrupted repair progress and a soloable path through every mandatory task. Give leaving the refuge a reason: visible jobs, optional supplies, and short risk/reward decisions. Measure the 15-second briefing, crew-tier expedition (150–240 seconds), extraction (60–90 seconds) and 10-second transit with real players. Test whether three stops produce variety through placement and killer combinations rather than repetitive chores. Preserve at least two plausible responses to ordinary pursuit; avoid compulsory dead ends and unavoidable spawn attacks. Art sessions 1 — Van and campfire: distressed company paint, protective lantern, awning, broad access, warm safe silhouette. Preserve zone, arrival, interaction, and navigation transforms. 2 — Killer identities: six strong silhouettes on a shared modest rig foundation. Keep visual weapon reach consistent with the simulation. Current procedural limb animation expects named arms/boots; replace deliberately if adding Animator rigs. Preserve attack warnings and hazard readability. 3 — Environment and sound: a modular cabin/garage kit, canopy, low-poly trees, shared atlas, and clear objective props. Replace synthesized warnings and decoy clicks with short original sounds; add restrained ambience and fire. Check voice-chat intelligibility and phone speakers. Asset budgets and authoring guardrails Current recorded geometry is 64,686 triangles across all loaded meshes , which includes the graybox layout variants and door frames. Initial mobile targets are below 70 MB download and about 250,000 visible world triangles; these are provisional, not frame-rate evidence. Start with a shared 1024-pixel atlas and simple materials. Prefer baked lighting, few transparent layers, limited particles/rigs/physics, and pooled supplies. There are 24 authored supply anchors per area; preserve compact solo eligibility and distinct reachable locations. Do not move protected zones, objective anchors, supply anchors, killer spawn points, patrol routes or the sixteen van and dispatch spawn spots accidentally when replacing meshes. Structural changes require navigation/lighting rebakes, scene validation, and all three platform builds. Add authors/licenses to credits when importing outside assets.

title: Development status
text: Current project status Gameplay expansion implemented and locally checked; not a release candidate. The September 20 update adds contribution-based rewards, quieter and occluded hearing, partial-cover visibility, warned lethal encounters, eighteen perks, ten consumables, five reusable tools, ten killers, optional salvage, generator recharge and persistent career titles. Capacity remains sixteen. Dispatch now has darker baked interior lighting, faulty fixtures, passable decorative furniture, fog, a corrected sign, a visible departure countdown, a five-second master-start hold and an illuminated lounge CRT with a fake projected glow. The creator accepted the darker lighting during development. Local editor and ClientSim results do not establish final physical-device or uploaded multiplayer acceptance. These notes are unlisted, public documentation . They are not linked from the player navigation or public search index. Do not put credentials, private playtester details, or raw logs here. Development-only spectator radar and AI diagnostics may change or be removed. How to read the status Implemented means the code and scene contain the feature. Locally checked means editor/static/ClientSim evidence exists. User confirmed identifies a reported uploaded playtest. Open means unfinished work or missing acceptance. These labels are deliberately not interchangeable. System register System Current state Remaining acceptance / work Single-contract rounds and persistent readiness Host starts ready players; new arrivals unready, choices persist; result returns to dispatch; current game host shown on the click control Uploaded multi-client host transfer and readiness, device input, economy pacing Three destinations and dispatch Deadwood, Last Chance and multilevel Calder are in rotation; dressed environments, protected van refuge and area fog Human route readability, mobile visibility/performance and final art acceptance Cargo, repairs, quotas, late entry Implemented; local checks. Repairs take 10 s of unbroken work and a generator has to be primed with the stop's fuel tank first Real concurrent work, disconnects, scaling transitions, and whether one tank per stop is enough traffic or too much Damage, rescue, all-down recovery Implemented; local checks; capture observed in uploaded play. Downed crew crawl in a forced prone pose, get a 20 s first bleed-out window and 10 s after, are revived automatically by nearby teammates over 10 s (25% shorter per extra rescuer), with 2 m acquisition / 4 m continuation and a paused bleed-out clock, and lose the respawn once a stop is past halfway The prone pose on a real avatar in a real client, group/solo fairness, and whether the late-stop lockout is the right pressure Ten killers and navigation Original six plus Hound, Mimic, Warden and Deadeye; five designated warned lethal attacks; local owner and replica checks Human fairness at 1–16 crew, warning readability and owner migration under latency Per-stop layouts and interactive doors Implemented; local layout/door lane with reachability verification Two-client door agreement, owner migration mid-stop, obstacles never trapping a player, the stop-start carve cost on Quest and iPhone Free briefing and spread spawn spots Hold retired 2026-09-24; 15 s since 2026-09-29, with the van boards closing after it; countdown, shop-window and spawn-ranking checks in the extended lane, board visibility in test-van-boards Leaving at any second on every device with no snap-back, countdown legibility, and spot spread with 2–8 real crew, and whether 15 s at the van is enough to shop Hearing, partial sight and search Quiet creeping, wall attenuation, distinct hearing ranges, head/torso samples, bounded evidence searches and Escape Artist/Trailbreaker interactions Natural desktop/roomscale evasion, avatar scales and party sizes Spectator map and remote killer model Shared feed and fixes implemented; local receiver/render checks Fresh non-owner and migration matrix; final radar policy Inventory, shop, shared loot Implemented; local transaction checks. Selling the equipped consumable refunds 50% bought / 25% found Real-client collection/purchase/sale races and interrupted grants Contribution XP, commendation milestones, eighteen perks Contribution rewards, saved reports, early point gains, specialist perks and paged menus implemented; local VM checks Human economy pacing and specialist combinations Career mastery and cosmetic titles Three job tracks plus ten killer tracks, three ranks each, saved earned title selection and crew roster display Human pacing, concurrent-instance and cloud-write acceptance Persistence and session wallets Restore/save paths implemented; legacy profile and pouch migration covered locally Uploaded reconnect, A → B → A, crash/save boundaries Ready/Watch and Force Start Shared departure countdown and separate five-second master hold with visible progress; local cancellation and input checks Simultaneous ready/cancel/departure and late join matrix Pass Host and AFK Claim Host User confirmed in uploaded play Offer decline/expiry, Keep Hosting, claimant departure, phase matrix Simulation ownership recovery Implemented; local fixtures Real suspension/departure during every transaction and AI mode Desktop controls and accessibility Implemented; creator has tested desktop Full shortcut/rebind/menu-interruption acceptance VR wrist/floating controls Implemented; the September 15 panel pass places the floating panel once, auto-closes it, and hides buttons that duplicate native controls Physical VR, handedness, seated and avatar-scale testing Touch controls Implemented; iPhone tried Discoverability, layout, touch ergonomics and Android phone tests Player capacity Sixteen retained at the creator's request; twenty/twenty-four-player expansion deferred Any future capacity increase needs its own policy and load testing Art, animation, sound, lighting Original specialist models and warning sounds; dressed map assets; baked moon occlusion; faulty lounge fixtures and CRT glow Headset presentation, mobile costs, final mix and credits Platform builds PC, Android, iOS SDK bundles successful Matching final uploads and physical platform verification Performance Current loaded geometry is 331,290 triangles; existing mobile recommendation warning retained 30-minute 1/16-player frame-time and memory captures Contest/release Planned Final rules/credits review, RC and manual submission Baseline snapshot Gameplay checkpoint: b7b741c — persistent career mastery and cosmetic crew titles , following the September 20 expansion milestones. Unity remains 2022.3.22f1 , VRChat SDK 3.10.5 , AI Navigation 1.1.5 . The shared editor scene contains other ongoing art/guide work; local source milestones deliberately preserve those changes rather than stage them wholesale. See testing and release gates for current lane dates, platform bundle evidence and limitations. Earlier September 15 totals are historical evidence, not a claim that every old lane ran again for this expansion. Next acceptance work Play the three-map loop with real crews, including all ten killers, optional salvage decisions and newly earned loadouts. Check quiet creeping, partial peeks, warned gunfire and physical cover on desktop and in roomscale VR. Exercise actual cloud saves, simultaneous interactions, late joins and owner departures under latency. Profile PCVR, Quest and iPhone with one and sixteen players; distinguish world costs from public-avatar costs. Judge economy pacing and mastery goals from ordinary play, then tune from those observations. Record uploaded test build, devices, party size and result before release. Detailed systems , AI , environment/art , roadmap , and publishing instructions are maintained separately.

title: Updating this site
text: Updating this site One normal project push The canonical website source lives at Docs/site/ in the main SpookCo repository. Edit the Markdown in Docs/site/content/ , commit it with the rest of the project, and push main . The Publish documentation GitHub Action builds and checks the site, then copies only the generated website into the separate kittynXR/spookco-docs repository. GitHub Pages serves that repository at spookco.kittyn.cat . There is an ignored local checkout at Docs/site-repo/ for inspecting the deployment repository. It is not a submodule and does not need to be committed from the game repo. Do not author content there: the next publish replaces generated pages. No Unity assets, client logs, player data, or game source are copied to the public docs repository. Editing map File or folder Purpose content/index.md Player landing-page copy content/guide/ Quick start, controls, equipment, progression, threats, FAQ content/internal/ Current status, systems, AI, art/design, roadmap, testing, publishing assets/site.css Shared responsive visual design assets/site.js Navigation/search enhancement assets/night-shift.svg Original decorative illustration, not a screenshot build.py Markdown rendering, templates, separate search indexes, sitemap check.py Broken links/anchors and public/internal separation checks requirements.txt Pinned Markdown dependency The existing engineering reports outside Docs/site/ remain project documentation. They are not blindly mirrored to the public site. Update the curated status/testing pages when a new result supersedes an older one. Label results as implemented, locally checked, user confirmed, or open; include the tested build and date when available. Preview locally From Docs/site/ , create a Python 3.12+ virtual environment, install requirements, then run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python build.py python check.py python -m http.server 8765 --directory _build --bind 127.0.0.1 Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and /internal/ . The build output and local environment are ignored by Git. The Action uses the same build/check commands before publication. Publishing and credentials The publishing Action runs for changes under Docs/site/** or its workflow, and can be run manually. It has read-only access to the main repo and uses a dedicated SSH deploy key with write access only to the docs repository. The private key is stored in the main repo’s SPOOKCO_DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY Actions secret. Never put its contents into source, Markdown, or logs. SSH host verification uses GitHub’s pinned Ed25519 host key. The docs repository publishes generated files from main at the repository root, with a .nojekyll file and CNAME containing spookco.kittyn.cat . Each deployment records the source revision in build-info.json . A failed build/check stops before replacing the deployed site; pushes are normal fast-forward updates with no force push. If publication fails, inspect the main repo’s Action first, then the docs repo’s Pages build/deployment. Confirm the deploy key still exists and the custom domain points to GitHub Pages. Cloudflare proxy/certificate changes can affect HTTPS independently of a successful site build. Public versus internal Player pages, player navigation, the public search index, and sitemap contain no links to /internal/ . Internal pages have their own navigation/search and noindex, nofollow metadata. This is discoverability separation, not authentication . Someone with the URL can read or share the pages, and the generated docs repository is public. Do not publish secrets or sensitive operational details here. If actual private team documentation becomes necessary, put it behind authentication instead of relying on an unlisted path. Platform references Publishing follows GitHub’s Pages publishing-source documentation , custom-domain setup , and deploy-key documentation .

title: Roadmap & open decisions
text: Roadmap & open decisions The September 20 gameplay and atmosphere expansion is implemented locally. Its remaining release work is uploaded multiplayer acceptance, physical input and presentation review, economy tuning and target-device profiling. Preserve the distinction between completed implementation and unmeasured human play. Next: make the stops distinct Review solo and group routes in all three destinations and the readability of safe refuge access. Paint the revamped van's livery, rust and stencils (paint brief in Docs/VanRevamp-2026-09-24.md); the walkable interior shipped on 2026-09-24. Measure whether completed-generator recharge, optional extraction salvage and mastery goals make work feel rewarding. The ten-second briefing hold read as a cage in playtests and was retired on 2026-09-24; watch whether the free 15-second briefing (shortened on 2026-09-29) still produces shared planning, and whether the spread spawn spots land people somewhere useful. Choose a cohesive palette, lighting mood, modular environment kit, and the ten killer silhouettes. Measure short-loop fun and pacing with ordinary players. Movement pressure now varies by killer and crew size; cover, doors, quiet movement, stale trails and committed firing lanes provide different responses. Tune from real play data. Then: finish integration and scale Keep capacity at sixteen; the creator deferred expansion to twenty or twenty-four players. Complete actual concurrent loot/purchase/cargo tests and reconnect A → B → A testing. Exercise ready countdown races, late entry, withdrawal, and quota reductions. Extend host-control testing beyond the user-confirmed Pass Host/AFK claim path to departures, cancellation, and suspension. Verify VR wrist/floating inventory, touch ergonomics, desktop direct shortcuts, and all accessibility alternatives. Then: balance, content freeze, and profiling Measure the revised early perk-point gains and longer-term mastery pacing before adopting an hours-to-unlock target. Test all ten killers with starter solo loadouts in all three destinations and with larger groups. Review charge/warp/hazard fairness, repeated stuns, and strong perk combinations. Complete art/audio, warning clarity, credits, dawn report polish, and the final status of spectator radar/AI diagnostics. Run 30-minute 1/16-player performance sessions, report world and public-avatar costs separately, and fix measured bottlenecks. Release targets The working plan targets a September 27, 2026 release candidate with a buffer before the planned October 1, 2026, 11:59:59 p.m. Pacific submission deadline. These are planning dates. Recheck the official contest rules, content requirements, and submission instructions before release; this site is not an eligibility ruling. Produce matching PC, Android, and iOS builds, review SDK warnings and credits, upload manually, and submit manually. Do not equate successful asset-bundle compilation with a released world or contest submission. Decisions still open Decision Why it matters Future capacity expansion Deferred; any increase beyond sixteen needs explicit scope, admission rules and performance evidence. Final spectator information Full sensing radar may undermine mystery; current display is useful for testing. Debug controls in release Determine whether to strip, gate, or retain diagnostics. Van interior versus exterior refuge Decided 2026-09-24: a walk-through interior (floor, roof, outer walls solid) inside the protected refuge; the covered exterior keeps the capacity. Solo/group pressure and economy Current numbers are initial tuning; measure fun and progression. The current per-killer pursuit ratios, crew scaling, warned lethal attacks, quiet-movement threshold and reward pacing need measurement against human evasion and ordinary play. End trip reward policy End trip deliberately ships unguarded for testing: play stop 1, return to dispatch, End trip, depart again, and that stop's objective, contract, extraction and rescue rewards pay again with freshly rolled supplies. The per-stop rate resembles a full run, so the gain is skipping stops 2–3 and the trip bonus rather than a rate exploit. Options: carry the ended trip's paid and claim masks forward for visited stops, put a cooldown on End trip, or accept it. Decide before release, and do not read progression pacing from sessions that used it. Free briefing The van hold was retired on 2026-09-24 ( Docs/BriefingHoldRemoval-2026-09-24.md ). Crew can now roam and pre-carry cargo and fuel for all 15 s (20 s before 2026-09-29) while the killer is dormant, reach the killer's fixed spawn before it appears, and the layout's re-roll window overlaps free crew. The clock was shortened to 15 s on 2026-09-29 and the van boards now close with it; watch whether crews still shop at the van. Final art/audio scope Keep three areas and ten identities achievable without increasing mobile cost excessively.

title: Systems & architecture
text: Systems & architecture The game-host role and simulation ownership are independent. Passing Host changes who can operate the lobby/round controls; the simulation owner keeps advancing gameplay without waiting for host input. Runtime boundaries Component Responsibility SpookRules Stable catalogue IDs, tuning, XP curve, pouch packing, quota and movement rules SpookSession Phases, deadlines, crew state, host offers/claims, health/recovery, trip choices, authored spawn-spot selection, and the briefing countdown SpookLedger Inventory/shop transactions, loot manifests and claims, rewards, cooldowns SpookProfile Restoration gate, permanent profile, bounded session wallets, accepted revision saves SpookObjectives Cargo reservation/carry/delivery, retained repairs, rescue work SpookKiller One native NavMesh agent, sensing, evidence/search, crew-scaled pursuit, attacks, durable AI checkpoint SpookLayout Per-stop obstacle rolls with reachability verification, and synchronized interactive door state SpookMapFeed Always-active shared killer/crew tracking and remote presentation snapshot SpookSpectatorMap Local map boards (dispatch and van), vision/hearing presentation, tracking age, crew names from the synced ledger slots, and the marker/roster picks SpookMapCamera Local click-to-watch camera: one disabled camera rendered by hand at 15 Hz into a render texture on the screen beside the picking board (the office window at dispatch; the CRT bezel on each field van's driver-side wall since batch 5), with fog/sky, killer-renderer and in-view screen brackets around each render (PC only for now) SpookControls Unified action routing, input priorities, saved device profiles SpookLoot At most 12 pooled shared supply objects; no per-pickup Update SpookEquipment Owner-checkpointed smoke, distractions, door braces, oil buffs and trip alarms; bounded pooled presentation SpookPanel / SpookFeedback Throttled UI, markers, interaction targets and alerts SpookTransition Local fade/teleport sequencing, replacement of obsolete destinations, and the leased black transit hold Authority and transactions Network entry points validate the actual caller, eligibility, and relevant revisions. A local click never grants an item. The ledger owner commits pouch changes and the shared claim in one synchronized object, with claimant/grant identity and duplicate protection. Full capacity rejects collection without claiming the pickup. Loot is rolled once per trip/stop. Restart Current Stop reuses the area, killer, manifest, and claims, but starts a clean objective attempt. Return to Dispatch keeps the trip open and records resumeStop , so the next departure resumes at that stop (or the next one if the stop was finished). Only the stop 3 report and the host's End Trip (phases 0–1) close a trip; the next departure after that is a fresh trip with new rolls. Every stop start bumps attemptSerial and clears that stop's field progress, while the once-per-trip objective and result reward masks prevent repeated payouts. Once-per-stop abilities and equipment cooldowns are also preserved. Transit between stops no longer teleports to the old van. Crew stay behind a black hold with locomotion paused, leased every session tick while phase 5 lasts plus a 5-second grace and a 20-second cap. The stop-start teleport runs under black and fades in over one second. Opening menus is refused during the hold. Selling the equipped consumable is a ledger transaction allowed in the same windows as buying. Bought supplies refund 50% and scavenged (found) supplies 25%; legacy pouches use bits 9–11 for found flags. New pouches set marker bit 15, use four bits per item, and store found flags in bits 12–14. Reads support both versions; a mutation migrates all three slots and provenance together. Empty remains zero. Sell descriptors use bit 4 for found provenance, separate from the item ID. The layout authority follows the simulation owner. Each stop attempt rolls one variant (or nothing) per authored site and an open/closed state per door, then verifies that every authored destination in the area is still reachable once the obstacles have carved navigation; it re-rolls twice before falling back to a clear field. Door toggles are owner-validated requests — able crew, within reach, in a running stop, not broken, past a cooldown, and with nobody in the doorway or the leaf's swing. An attempt first seen mid-stop adopts a clear field rather than dropping obstacles around players. Initial quotas and loot counts use the participating-player snapshot. Joins do not increase active quotas or supplies. Departures, withdrawal, and sustained suspension may lower outstanding requirements without erasing finished work. If nobody remains active, return to the lobby without completion rewards. Temporary equipment effects The equipment authority follows the session owner and checkpoints 32 shared effect slots, source player IDs, absolute expiry times and the attempt serial. Oil also records the owner identity per crew slot. A new attempt invalidates old effects, and reused crew slots cannot inherit oil. Receivers reconstruct local pooled visuals and positional alarm audio from synchronized state; no new networked objects are spawned per use. Smoke intersects both head and torso visibility segments, including close contact, without suppressing hearing or physical attack resolution. Braces add one four-second normal door-breach delay; crew opening and charge destruction clear them. Flash bulbs and alarms share the camera stun immunity; bolts share decoy resistance. Battery use requires an active gear cooldown and cannot stack armed alarms. Invalid effects return false before the ledger spends an item. Useful interruption rewards reuse the existing bounded support grant. Briefing countdown and spawn placement The 15-second briefing (shortened from 20 s on 2026-09-29) is free: the van hold that kept each client's own crew member inside the refuge for the first ten seconds was retired on 2026-09-24 (see Docs/BriefingHoldRemoval-2026-09-24.md ). No walls, marker, pull-back or lease remain; crew may leave at any second. _BriefingCountdown() shows the countdown only while the phase is briefing, the local slot is alive crew and the synced deadline is plausible (0 < remaining <= briefingSeconds + 2 ); a stale or absurd deadline shows nothing. The HUD and status read "BRIEFING — shop at the van or head out (Ns)" and the wrist "BRIEFING Ns". Shopping and selling are gated by _Shopping (briefing inside the refuge, or dispatch); pickups are open through the briefing while delivery, priming and generator work wait for the expedition. The field vans' Shop + Inventory and Perk selection boards show only during the briefing and go blank at the phase flip; the personal menu keeps the inventory actions in the field. User layer 22 stays reserved as SpookWorldBuilder.GuardLayer (players collide, the descriptor's Interact Passthrough bit 0 is set) for invisible walkway guards; world visuals live on DecorLayer (0) and only eye-locked veils, banners and prone seats on OverlayLayer (2). Game-driven moves no longer stack the crew on one point. Sixteen authored, ground-seated spots sit under each van anchor and sixteen at dispatch, 1.5 m apart, clear of solid geometry, inside the refuge's .85 m spawn inset and facing the anchor's direction. They are used by transit arrival, stop start, restart, resume, late join, manual respawn at the refuge, recovery return, Watch, return to dispatch and the report. The local spot index is the player's rank by ledger slot — among crew for a van, among registered players for dispatch — where rank 0 keeps the original anchor, so solo positions are unchanged, and higher ranks map into spots 1–15 without ever wrapping back onto the anchor. Missing spot data falls back to the anchor, and VRChat's own join spawn still uses the single descriptor spawn. Two overlaps are accepted: more than 16 eligible players re-using spots 1–15 and a late joiner landing on a spot a teammate still occupies. A spectator who respawns during a trip stays on the world spawn at dispatch and is never moved to the van. A first-half recovery lands instead at the nearest recovery stone inside the stop's tier when one is nearer than the van ( Docs/RecoveryStones-2026-09-24.md ); the stones are shown only in phases 2–3 of the current area, inside the tier and before halfway ( _LateInStop ), and _RecoveryPost returns -1 after halfway so a vanished stone never receives anyone. Persistence Wait for OnPlayerRestored before writes, purchases, and grants. The permanent profile holds XP, commendations, perk selection, reusable gear, and player identity token. Separate VR/desktop/touch keys hold controls. A synchronized random live-session key survives trips, resets, role changes, and ordinary ownership migration. A bounded 128-record history stores session cash, pouch, cooldowns, inventory revisions, grant identity, and reward masks. The current wallet is updated during play; the history index changes only on session entry/eviction. Old prototype wallet data has a migration path. The implemented goal is same-session rejoin and A → B → A restoration without duplicated loot or refunded consumption. Actual cloud timing, interrupted writes, and concurrent-client race behavior remain uploaded acceptance work. No departure callback can guarantee a final cloud write after an abrupt crash. Stable content IDs Areas: 0 Camp Deadwood, 1 Last Chance Service Station, 2 Calder Nuclear Laboratory (draft, not in normal trips). Killers: 0 Groundskeeper, 1 Rattletrap, 2 Roadkill, 3 Hitchhiker, 4 Usher, 5 Switchboard. Consumables: 0 empty, 1 ration, 2 soda, 3 flare, 4 tape, 5 smoke, 6 bolts, 7 brace, 8 oil, 9 flash bulb, 10 battery. Reusable gear: 0 decoy, 1 camera, 2 EMF pager, 3 track shoes, 4 trip alarm. Display order follows unlock thresholds without changing stable IDs. Perk bits 0–18: Spotter, Courier, Mechanic, Field Medic, Scrapper, Soft Soles, Adrenaline, Quickdraw, Hardhat, Second Wind, Silent Tools, Ear Defenders, Escape Artist, Braced, Clear Lenses, Sixth Sense, Trailbreaker, Inspector, Focused Beam (level 15, added 2026-09-23). The perk pages size themselves from the catalogue, nine rows each, and the career mastery pages follow them. The ten legacy indices and costs are unchanged. _SanitizePerks validates levels and budget while retaining affordable selections. Preserve IDs when replacing art or changing display names. Three consumable slots allow duplicates. Old three-bit IDs migrate to the marked four-bit format on mutation. XP to the next level is 150 + 35 × (current level − 1) through level 40; 31,785 total XP. Final reward pacing has not been measured. Capacity and transport limits Runtime admission is still 16 despite several storage/feed arrays having 32 slots. The capacity increase is deferred. Larger storage arrays do not raise the admission cap. The AI checkpoint and presentation stream are separate. The always-active manual feed requests updates at 4 Hz; matching trip/stop/area/revision is required. A new owner can recover from a fresher presentation pose under a recovery interval. Local decoding/interpolation tests do not prove Photon delivery or suspension recovery. Generator power Completed repair bits enable a six-metre, solid-geometry-occluded connection during expedition and extraction. The shared ledger owner samples able players with active gear every 0.25 seconds and subtracts one extra second per elapsed second from their existing absolute cooldown deadline. Two consecutive eligible samples bind to the same player and cooldown; attempts, phases and owner changes discard elapsed history. A sample contributes at most 0.5 seconds. Multiple generators do not stack. Cooldown-only changes use the existing manual ledger snapshot without increasing inventory transaction revisions. The profile writer compares the saved cooldown as well as the revision so those snapshots persist. Power changes no rewards, health, contract quota, deadline or armed-alarm placement limits. Optional salvage The cargo pool has nineteen independent slots: required cases 0–15 and bonus cases 16–18. SpookObjectives checkpoints three bonus counts and nine area-local layout indices. On each stop it selects one, two or three distinct eligible anchors at least ten metres from the van for initial crews of 1–2, 3–8 or 9–16. Same-layout retries retain those choices. Bonus pickup opens only during completed-contract extraction and closes at the existing deadline. Delivery maps the three bonus slots to ledger objective bits 26–28; required cargo, repair and fuel bits remain unchanged. The once-per-trip paid mask also hides already-paid bonuses after an attempt restart. Delivery pays twice crew-scaled cargo XP and $24, with existing identity-bound handoff credit and Scrapper rounding. Cargo pickup and delivery require aligned objectives, session and ledger authority. The first eight seconds of completed extraction defer the all-aboard check while unpaid bonus work is available. This does not move the deadline, and everybody can still choose an early departure. Gold straps, case stencils, the extraction banner and HUD/wrist counts explain the option. Physical pickups and hands-free actions use the existing cargo routing. Contribution accounting Movement no longer calls participation. Cargo and repair use identity-bound shared contribution records; cargo needs a three-metre carry and repair helpers need 10% progress. Fuel priming has separate paid bits 21–25. The ledger's once-per-trip objective claim bounds finisher and helper awards together, including retries. Bounded rescue and real gear interruption remain independent paid categories. A completed, contributed contract awards one commendation, and extracting alive from it adds one. Failed extraction does not pay a survival bonus. Eliminated contributors can receive contract credit. Final-shift XP/cash scales with the player's earned contract bits. The permanent sp key and balance are preserved; only the player-facing name changes. Current-attempt report arrays synchronize work/contract/extraction/shift XP, cash and commendations. Compact wallet fields ra , ro and rs preserve that report on a same-attempt reconnect. Career mastery The ledger synchronizes 13 counters per identity in mastery[416] : hauling, engineering, support and the ten killers. careerTitle[32] selects none (0) or track + 1. Job thresholds are 5/25/100; killer thresholds are 3/10/25. Titles are cosmetic roster text, with owner-validated selection through ledger action 8 and UI action 44. The existing perk navigator retains core/specialist pages and adds two career pages on every panel. Credits are inside the same paid objective/support/extraction transaction and revision as their existing rewards. Objective helpers receive one mastery credit; support retains separate once-per-stop rescue and useful-gear bits. Killer credit requires the contributed extraction award. Paid masks survive stop retries. A newly ended trip retains the existing fresh-trip reward policy; this change does not impose a new replay restriction. The permanent sc.profile.v1 dictionary adds a 13-number mastery list and title selection. Older killer masks migrate one proven escape per bit, without invented job history. Counts clamp to 0..1,000,000; malformed entries become zero. Reused slots replace all counters, while a returning cached identity merges each counter by maximum, matching existing permanent XP restoration. Simultaneous independent instances are not an additive distributed counter; uploaded concurrent-instance acceptance remains necessary. Progress is saved only after the owner snapshot is sent, alongside the existing wallet revision.

title: Testing & release gates
text: Testing & release gates Current implementation: September 20, 2026 gameplay and atmosphere expansion. The new milestone and final integration evidence below supersedes the old baseline for changed behavior. Each ClientSim lane runs in a fresh local session; these are actual Udon paths with controlled fixtures, not real Photon transport, uploaded cloud saves or physical-input acceptance. September 20 expansion evidence Focused lane Started UTC Passing assertions Quiet/occluded hearing and partial visibility 14:47:30 48 Warned lethal encounters and next-stop recovery 14:48:16 21 Four specialist killers, map/tier entry and counterplay 16:26:46 192 Expanded consumables and reusable gear 17:43:45 253 Completed-generator recharge 17:42:50 69 Optional extraction salvage 18:11:48 110 Perks and career navigation regression 18:38:12 316 Persistent mastery, title selection and sixteen-player roster 18:40:26 511 Contribution and saved-result regression 18:41:10 66 These 1,586 focused assertions were run as their milestones landed. They are not all rerun after every later edit. The final integration lanes additionally exercise the combined loop and receiver/registration behavior; precise current evidence is recorded in the gameplay expansion audit. The full starter-loadout trip completes Calder, Deadwood and Last Chance through normal objective RPCs. With no optional salvage it banks 290 XP, $156, six commendations, six hauling credits, six engineering credits and three killer-escape credits . The fixture pauses the killer and accelerates deadlines to isolate task, travel and reward integration; separate encounter lanes test threat behavior. Mastery restoration checks include real remote ClientSim PlayerData, delayed restoration, duplicate identities, late joins, cached rejoin and saved title unlocks. Replica checks encode/decode SDK snapshots for all ten killer presentations across three maps. These narrow claims do not establish transport reliability under real latency. Fresh PC, Android and iOS SDK bundles include the complete runtime expansion. Platform sizes and hashes are recorded in the final gameplay audit. These are world asset bundles, not standalone applications, and successful compilation does not establish device frame rate. Final combined integration and bundles Lane Started UTC, September 20 Passing checks Complete three-map trip with contribution/mastery totals 18:51:39 56 Remote registration, late join and cached career restoration 18:54:11 25 Ten-killer replica presentation and ownership 18:55:04 225 Broad economy, input, phases and owner recovery 18:56:10 340 All 646 passed. Final lobby (33), atmosphere (44), CRT (11) and whole-scene structural checks also passed. The conservative loaded mesh count is 331,290 triangles, retaining the existing mobile recommendation warning. Current SDK bundle Bytes Build started UTC StandaloneWindows64 13,887,391 19:01:02 Android 20,158,088 18:47:59 iOS 20,050,244 18:49:10 All succeeded against the complete production runtime; intervening final-pass changes were editor tests and documentation only. The editor was returned to PC. No upload or site publication was performed. Human reports The creator reports that the basic loop works and the current killers are a useful baseline. Pass Host and AFK timeout / Claim Host have been tested in uploaded play. Desktop and iPhone have been tried. Earlier reports drove fixes for stalled pursuit, non-owner registration/tracking, desktop pointer/menu behavior, and sensing-outline visibility. These reports do not close every killer, device, and networking case. The held-W issue was attributed by the creator to the KVM setup and does not occur with the physical keyboard; no game-side keyboard workaround is required for that report. Historical September 15 baseline lanes Lane Started UTC Passing assertions Scene/rules validation 2026-09-16 00:09:47 554 Local gameplay 2026-09-16 00:10:46 68 Extended local integration 2026-09-16 00:12:18 220 Menu and travel presentation 2026-09-16 00:15:16 76 Killer pressure, layouts, doors 2026-09-16 00:15:48 79 Killer movement watchdog 2026-09-16 00:17:30 13 Warning-to-pursuit 2026-09-16 00:19:32 4 Crew registration 2026-09-16 00:20:13 23 Movement hearing / search 2026-09-16 00:20:40 99 AI review / diagnostics 2026-09-16 00:22:17 37 Corner pursuit 2026-09-16 00:24:19 12 Spectator map / negative clock 2026-09-16 00:24:56 143 Non-owner tracking receiver 2026-09-16 00:25:23 104 Killer replica/movement 2026-09-16 00:25:44 87 1,519 assertions across structural scene validation and thirteen ClientSim lanes, every lane passing. Structural checks, explicit SDK delegates, and single-VM ClientSim fixtures cover actual Udon paths where possible. Receiver decoding tests and rendering tests are useful but are not real Photon transport, cloud restoration, or physical input proof. The scene lane reports 64,686 triangles across all loaded world meshes , three non-directional lightmaps, 197/197 static renderers with baked lightmap indices , and 693 Udon behaviours including static UI handlers, the layout authority with its eight doors, and the editor-only validation fixture. None of those counts establishes Udon CPU cost or frame rate. It also covers the spawn-spot layout (anchor identity, offsets, ground seating, capsule clearance, spacing and refuge containment), the absence of retired briefing-hold nodes, the guard-layer (22) collision row and the descriptor's Interact Passthrough bit, every collected layout site and door, obstacles keeping clear of anchors and the refuge, and baked navigation running through each doorway while its frame stays solid. The historical pressure lane measured patrol and pursuit speeds for the original six killers at crew 1 and crew 8 through the real owner loop, the lunge and its cooldown, the recovery after a landed hit, crew and killer door handling with their refusals, eight layout rolls with reachability verification and a clear-field fallback, runtime navigation carving, and the spectator map's obstacle and door markers. The extended lane's BriefingFreedomChecks covers the free briefing (the hold was retired on 2026-09-24): no barrier objects under any van root, the countdown on wrist and HUD, leaving in the first second with no pull-back and no notice, shopping refused in the field and accepted at the van, the silent hide on an implausible deadline, recovering, watcher and late-join behaviour, a restart landing free on the spot, and the countdown ending on expedition. Since 2026-09-29 its fixtures follow rules.briefingSeconds (15 s) and a host restart is checked to run a full 15 s briefing. The separate test-van-boards lane checks through compiled Udon that both field-van boards show only during the briefing, close at the phase flip (also on a mid-expedition load), reopen at the next briefing on the shop page, and that the warehouse boards never close. The smoke lane checks that a solo crew can leave immediately after arrival. Raw logs remain local/ignored; this public site publishes summaries only. Historical September 14–15 SDK bundles Platform Bytes Written UTC PC 2,923,464 2026-09-15 23:28:34 Android / Quest 2,310,266 2026-09-14 02:46:23 iOS 2,248,548 2026-09-14 02:48:28 The PC bundle was rebuilt after the killer pressure, layout and door pass, which also confirms the SDK accepts their carving navigation obstacles and bake-exclusion markers in a world build; it is smaller than the September 14 bundle because the non-directional lightmap fix and the geometry changes both affect it. It predates the briefing-hold pass, and the Android and iOS bundles predate both September 15 passes. These are VRChat world asset bundles, not standalone executables or exact client download/memory measurements. Reviewed non-blocking warnings include the mobile quality profile allowing multiple pixel lights (authored lights are baked), and an inapplicable iPhone C++ compiler option for this bundle workflow. Profile actual mobile lighting rather than dismissing the warning permanently. Uploaded test matrix still needed Complete normal trips with 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, and 16 participants; all ten killers, all three areas, starter solo loadout. Ready/unready cancellation, Force Start, simultaneous departure, late entry, and 8 → 2 / 2 → 1 / 1 → 8 scaling without raised quotas or rerolled loot. Solo/all-down recovery, rescues, interrupted repairs, Second Wind, and safe refuge behavior. Several clients claiming one supply; full pouch; concurrent purchases; duplicate requests/grants; accessible and native cargo contention. Rejoin after earning, purchasing, scavenging, swapping, consuming, and using cooldowns; A → B → A; crashes during grants/saves. Host offer expiry/decline, Keep Hosting, meaningful activity cancellation, claimant/host departure, and ownership suspension in every phase. Non-owner map/model agreement, late snapshots, owner migration during charge/warp/stun/gun commitment, and effects/hits under latency. Chase balance at 1, 2, 4, 8 and a full lobby for every killer: whether distance alone still escapes, whether cover, doors and the van read as the answers, and whether any chase feels unavoidable rather than merely hard. Interactive doors with at least two clients: opening and closing from both sides, the refusal cases, a door slammed in a pursuing hunter's face breaking for the rest of the stop, agreement for late joiners and after owner migration, and nobody pushed or trapped by a swinging leaf. Per-stop layouts: obstacles differ between stops, never block an anchor or trap a player, the hunter paths around them, and a spectator sees the same field as the crew. Every direct/button alternative, both hands/wrists, seated/scale differences, menu interruptions, rebinding, profile persistence, and no unintended consumption or cargo drops. The VR panel pass: floating mode level and not in the face, tab switching never moving it, the three-metre auto-close, the launcher below the wrist staying clear of Close, Recenter, auto-close on expedition start, cargo grab and a hit, and the glance wrist card with alerts still visible; the stick ring equipping each entry outright in both hands' settings. The free briefing in a headset with 2–8 crew: leaving the refuge at any second with no wall, strip or snap-back, readable countdown text on every device, shopping at the van during the 15 s briefing, both side-door boards going blank at the flip, and refusal in the field, spectators and downed crew unaffected, and a stalled or implausible deadline hiding the countdown quietly. Spread spawns with real crews: no two players on one spot at departure or arrival, spots facing the van, and only the accepted overlaps (over 16 eligible players, a spectator at the plain anchor, a late joiner on an occupied spot). Trip resume: return to dispatch mid-stop and depart again, expecting a full attempt with no pre-done objectives and no second payout; End trip only at dispatch or during the countdown. End trip reward replay ships deliberately unguarded for testing, so progression pacing must not be read from sessions that used it. Hardware and performance Available: Linux PCVR with RTX 3090; Windows AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700; Quest 3; iPhone 16 Pro. Other testers can cover standalone Android phones. Confirm the exact PC headset and refresh rate when scheduling performance acceptance. Run 30-minute sessions with one and sixteen controlled lightweight avatars. Targets: PCVR 90 FPS, Quest 3 72 FPS, iPhone 16 Pro 60 FPS . Capture CPU/Udon and GPU frame time, batches, memory, textures/lightmaps, and bundle/download cost. Report public-avatar overhead separately. No current count or build result certifies these targets. Local commands Tools/Gameplay.ps1 adds the focused expansion commands hearing , lethal , rewards , perks , items , encounters , generator-power , bonus , mastery and the lobby/CRT patch and validation commands. Use the existing Unity editor and fixed-command bridge; do not launch a second editor for the same project. Tools/SpookCo.ps1 exposes status , refresh , reload-scene , compile , validate , patch-scene , clientsim , stop , smoke , extended , presentation , pressure , movement , pursuit , ai-review , corners , hearing , map-clock , remote-map , registration , replica , probe , bake , capture commands, and the platform build commands. Use a fresh ClientSim run per test lane. An asynchronous command acknowledgment is not completion: require a fresh result log ending in SUCCESS. Do not modify scripts during a build/test. World uploads and contest submission remain manual.
